title: Mitotic phenomena follow from simple physical assumptions and have secondary significance

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Mitotic phenomena follow from simple physical assumptions and have secondary significance

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Most if not all of the intracellular phenomena of mitosis follow inevitably from very simple assumptions about the physical constitution of the cell and a simple distribution of polarised forces within it, and are likely to prove of only remote and secondary biological significance.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IV: On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Most, if not all of them, would seem to follow immediately and inevitably from very simple assumptions as to the physical constitution of the cell, and from an extremely simple distribution of polarised forces within it.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IV, “On the Internal Form and Structure of the Cell”; topic “Biological significance of mitotic figures”. Scope: intracellular phenomena of cell division in plants and animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch04-12: not-empirically-resolvable, resolvability 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Many mitotic observations are measurable, but the claim combines an unspecified physical model with a judgment about significance. Without a formal model, almost any outcome can be accommodated by changing the assumed forces.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The physical-sufficiency portion could be evaluated only after specifying the assumptions and predicted phenomena, but the assertion of 'remote and secondary biological significance' has no objective decision criterion.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Neither the simple assumptions nor the full phenomenon set are specified.

Biological significance is a context-dependent evaluative category.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Whether a simple force picture can generate mitotic geometry is a modelling question already tied to other claims in the chapter. The further statement that those phenomena are biologically secondary does not name an observation that would be absent if mitosis were functionally important. Datasets of mitotic diversity cannot settle that wording.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim says mitotic figures follow from simple physical assumptions and therefore have only remote biological significance. A physical model that fits the figures would not measure significance, and a biologically important mitotic step can still be physically simple.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Secondary biological significance is a judgment, not a variable.

Sufficiency of a physical model does not separate functional from incidental mitotic detail.
